title: Count Primes
summary: For a given integer n, calculate and return the count of prime numbers that are less than n.
statement: For a given integer n, calculate and return the count of prime numbers that are less than n.
constraints: Count primes STRICTLY LESS than n. Zero and one are not prime; a prime equal to n is excluded.
hints: Instead of testing every candidate independently, let each prime eliminate its multiples.
Maintain a compact prime-candidate array for values below n.
For each surviving p with p²<n, clear p²,p²+p,… below n; count remaining candidates after excluding 0 and 1.
Starting at p² is valid because smaller composite multiples already have a smaller prime factor.
editorial: The sieve of Eratosthenes marks composites by prime factors. Byte storage and stepped slice marking keep the maximum input practical in Pyodide. The independent oracle trial-divides each small candidate through its integer square root. A separate Euler linear-sieve regression verifies the full 5000000 boundary count, 348513, rather than relying only on the reference to supply that expected result.

tests.explanation: Although 2 is prime, it is not strictly less than itself, so the answer is 0.
